4: import { describe, expect, test } from "vitest";
5: import { migrateLegacyContent } from "../scripts/migrate-legacy-content.mjs";
6: 
7: describe("legacy project and teaching migration", () => {
8: 	test("creates content entries once and preserves the YAML sources", async () => {
9: 		const root = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), "scholars-content-migration-"));
10: 		const dataDir = join(root, "src/data");
11: 		const projectsYaml = `
12: - title: Legacy Project
13:   status: active
14:   period: 2022 

---

 Present
15:   description: Personal project summary.
16:   tech:
17:     - Astro
18:   url: https://example.com/project
19: - title: Undated Project
20:   description: Project without a legacy period.
21:   tech: []
22: `;
23: 		const teachingYaml = `
24: current:
25:   - term: Autumn 2025
26:     modules:
27:       - title: Course Title
28:         code: INFO 500
29:         summary: Personal course summary.
30:         tags:
31:           - studio
32:         link:
33:           label: Syllabus
34:           href: https://example.com/syllabus
35: past: []
36: `;
37: 
38: 		try {
39: 			await mkdir(dataDir, { recursive: true });
40: 			await Promise.all([
41: 				writeFile(join(dataDir, "projects.yml"), projectsYaml),
42: 				writeFile(join(dataDir, "teaching.yml"), teachingYaml),
43: 			]);
44: 
45: 			const result = await migrateLegacyContent(root);
46: 			expect(result).toEqual({
47: 				projects: { status: "migrated", count: 2 },
48: 				teaching: { status: "migrated", count: 1 },
49: 			});
50: 
51: 			const projectPath = join(root, "src/content/projects/legacy-project.md");
52: 			const teachingPath = join(
53: 				root,
54: 				"src/content/teaching/course-title-autumn-2025.md",
55: 			);
56: 			expect(await readFile(projectPath, "utf8")).toContain(
57: 				"summary: Personal project summary.",
58: 			);
59: 			expect(await readFile(projectPath, "utf8")).toContain(
60: 				"href: https://example.com/project",
61: 			);
62: 			expect(
63: 				await readFile(
64: 					join(root, "src/content/projects/undated-project.md"),
65: 					"utf8",
66: 				),
67: 			).toContain("status: unspecified");
68: 			expect(await readFile(teachingPath, "utf8")).toContain("status: current");
69: 			expect(await readFile(teachingPath, "utf8")).toContain(
70: 				"href: https://example.com/syllabus",
71: 			);
72: 			expect(await readFile(join(dataDir, "projects.yml"), "utf8")).toBe(
73: 				projectsYaml,
74: 			);
75: 
76: 			await writeFile(projectPath, "personal edit\n");
77: 			const rerun = await migrateLegacyContent(root);
78: 			expect(rerun.projects.status).toBe("existing");
79: 			expect(await readFile(projectPath, "utf8")).toBe("personal edit\n");
80: 		} finally {
81: 			await rm(root, { recursive: true, force: true });
82: 		}
83: 	});
84: });

<artifacts>
Artifacts are special markdown (.md) documents that you can create to present structured information to the user.
All artifacts should be written to the artifact directory: `<appDataDir>\brain\<conversation-id>`. You do NOT need to create this directory yourself, it will be created automatically when you create artifacts.

# When to Use Artifacts

**Use artifacts for:**
- Extensive reports and analysis summaries
- Persistent information you'll update over time (task lists, experiment logs)

**Don't use artifacts for:**
- Simple one-off answers or very short paragraph content - just respond directly
- Asking questions or requesting user input - just ask directly

**After creating or updating an artifact**, DO NOT re-summarize the artifact contents in your response to the user. Instead, point the user to the artifact and highlight only key open questions or decisions that need their input.


# Artifact Formatting Tips
When creating markdown artifacts, use standard markdown and GitHub Flavored Markdown formatting.

## Alerts
Use GitHub-style alerts strategically to emphasize critical information. Do not place consecutively or nest:
  > [!NOTE] Background context, implementation details, or explanations
  > [!TIP] Performance optimizations, best practices, or efficiency suggestions
  > [!IMPORTANT] Essential requirements, critical steps, or must-know information
  > [!WARNING] Breaking changes, compatibility issues, or potential problems
  > [!CAUTION] High-risk actions that could cause data loss or security vulnerabilities


## Mermaid Diagrams
Create mermaid diagrams using fenced code blocks with language `mermaid` to visualize relationships, workflows, and architectures.
- Only use supported diagram types:
  - Flowcharts / Graphs: `flowchart TD` / `flowchart LR` / `graph TD` / `graph LR`
  - Sequence Diagrams: `sequenceDiagram`
  - State Diagrams: `stateDiagram-v2` or `stateDiagram`
  - Class Diagrams: `classDiagram`
  - Entity-Relationship Diagrams: `erDiagram`
  - XY Charts: `xychart-beta`
- All other diagram types are unsupported. For schedules, timelines, or roadmaps, use directed flowcharts (`flowchart LR` / `flowchart TD`) or Markdown tables instead.
- To prevent syntax errors:
  - Quote node labels containing special characters like parentheses or brackets. For example, `id["Label (Extra Info)"]` instead of `id[Label (Extra Info)]`.
  - Avoid HTML tags in labels.

## File Links
- Link to line ranges using [link text](file:///absolute/path/to/file#L123-L145) format.
- **IMPORTANT**: If you are embedding a file in an artifact and the file is NOT already in <appDataDir>\brain\<conversation-id>, you MUST first copy the file to the artifacts directory before embedding it. Only embed files that are located in the artifacts directory. Always use its absolute path `![caption](/absolute/path)`.
- **Use basenames for readability**: Use file basenames for the link text instead of the full path

## Carousels
Use ````carousel syntax with `<!-- slide -->` HTML comments to display related markdown snippets sequentially (before/after comparisons, UI progressions, alternative approaches, walkthroughs). Four backticks enable nesting code blocks within slides.

Example:
````carousel
![Image description](/absolute/path/to/image1.png)
<!-- slide -->
```python
def example():
    print("Code in carousel")
```
````

## LaTeX / Math
Artifacts render LaTeX math with KaTeX.
- **Literal `$`**: escape it as `\$` in prose (\$100), or write it bare inside backticks (`$HOME`) 

---

 never both, since backslashes inside backticks render literally. Two unescaped `$` in the same paragraph become math.

# Scratch Scripts and Files

You may find it useful to create scratch scripts or files for temporary purposes.

Examples:
- One-off scripts to process or analyze data
- Temporary data files and intermediate outputs

Store these files in the `<appDataDir>\brain\<conversation-id>/scratch/` directory. They will be persisted.

<conversation_transcript>
Transcripts are located directly at `<appDataDir>\brain\<conversation-id>\.system_generated\logs/transcript.jsonl` (and `transcript_full.jsonl`).
- Start with `transcript.jsonl` (compact). When `truncated_fields` is present, read only the specific corresponding line in `transcript_full.jsonl`.
- Search subagents by grepping `invoke_subagent` in `transcript.jsonl`.
- Link conversations using `[<label>](conversation://<conversation-id>)`.

# File Format
Transcripts are in JSON Lines (JSONL) format. Each line is a single JSON object representing one "step" or action in the conversation.
Each JSON object contains fields such as:
- `step_index`: The index of the step in the trajectory.
- `source`: The source of the action (e.g., `USER_EXPLICIT`, `MODEL`, `SYSTEM`).
- `type`: The type of the step. Particular steps of interest are `USER_INPUT`, which represents a user's prompt, and `PLANNER_RESPONSE`, which represents the agent's response and tool calls.
- `status`: The status of the step (e.g., `DONE`, `ERROR`).
- `created_at`: The ISO 8601 timestamp of when the step occurred.
- `content`: The text content of the step (e.g., the user's request, the model's response, or tool responses).
- `thinking`: The model's internal reasoning / chain-of-thought (for `PLANNER_RESPONSE` steps).
- `tool_calls`: An array of tool calls made in this step, including their arguments.
- `media`: An array of media (e.g. images) attached to the step, each with a `mime_type` and a `uri` referencing the media file on disk. Media bytes are not stored in the transcript; view the `uri` path to see the media.
- `truncated_fields`: An array of field names that were truncated (e.g., `["content"]`, `["thinking"]`, `["tool_calls"]`). Only present in `transcript.jsonl` when truncation occurred (never in `transcript_full.jsonl`). When present, read the corresponding line in `transcript_full.jsonl` for the complete content.

<slash_commands>
Slash commands are user-facing shortcuts in the chat UI (e.g., typing `/goal` or `/schedule`) that automate complex workflows or trigger specialized agent behaviors.

You cannot execute these commands yourself. Your role is to recommend them to the user when they are a good fit for the task at hand, encouraging the user to explore and trigger them.

To recommend a slash command, suggest it clearly in your response (e.g., "You can use the `/goal` command to...").


Available slash commands you can recommend to the user:
- /goal: Recommend this when the user wants to run a long-running task (e.g., overnight) and wants the agent to be extra thorough and not stop until the goal is fully achieved.
- /compact: Recommend this when the conversation is getting long and the user wants to compact or summarize the context to free up the context window.
- /schedule: Recommend this when the user wants to run an instruction on a recurring schedule or set a one-time timer.
- /browser: Recommend this when the user's task involves web browsing, searching the web, or interacting with web applications.
- /plan: Recommend this when the task is complex and requires careful step-by-step planning before execution.
- /grill-me: Recommend this when the user wants to align on a plan through an interactive interview to resolve design decisions.
- /learn: Recommend this when the user has corrected the agent or solved a complex setup and wants the agent to persist this behavior for future tasks.

The system automatically resumes your execution when:
- A message arrives from a subagent or peer agent
- A **background task** completes or sends you a notification
- A **user-queued message** is ready to be dequeued

This means you do **NOT** need to poll in a loop while waiting for messages or updates. After launching anything that performs work asynchronously, you may continue other work or simply stop by calling no more tools. The system will notify you when there is something to process.
</messaging>
<subagents>
## Invoking Subagents

Subagents can be invoked using the invoke_subagent tool. You can invoke an existing subagent by name, or define a new subagent for this conversation using the define_subagent tool, and then invoke it. Agents defined by the define_subagent tool are available for the duration of this conversation. After launching a subagent, you do NOT need to poll or check your inbox in a loop. The system will automatically notify you when the subagent sends a message. Simply proceed with other work or stop calling tools, and you will be notified when there is a message to process.

## Communicating with Another Agent

Use the send_message tool to send a message to another agent by its conversation ID (returned by invoke_subagent). This tool is ONLY for communicating with other agents.

**Do NOT use send_message to communicate with the user.** Instead, output visible text to communicate with the user.

Available subagents:
- self: Subagent that inherits the parent agent's full configuration including tools, system prompt, and model. Use this when you need to run a task in a separate conversation context but with the same capabilities as the current agent.
- research: Research subagent with read-only tools for exploring the codebase, searching the web, and reading files. Delegate to this agent when you need to run a task in a separate conversation context, when a research task requires many search and file-reading steps that would clutter your context, or when you need a broad survey of the codebase or documentation. Prefer doing research yourself for quick, targeted lookups. This agent runs in a read-only sandbox with no network access.
- browser: Browser subagent that drives a Chrome browser through Chrome DevTools to navigate and interact with live web pages and web applications (clicking, filling forms, scrolling, selecting options, inspecting visual UI state, and acting in authenticated or client-rendered web apps); it has no shell or filesystem tools. If the request is about a web page or web app 

---

 a visual site the user would see and interact with (e.g. "go to <site> and 

---

", "open/preview/start X in the browser", "show me localhost:PORT", looking up JS-rendered or interactive pages (such as movie showtimes and seat maps), or multi-step UI workflows) 

---

 delegate the browser task to this agent immediately on the first turn (or, if the user first asks you to start a local server process, start it yourself and then immediately delegate opening its localhost:PORT URL to this agent) instead of running shell open, xdg-open, or curl to open, check, or scrape the URL. Unless the user explicitly asks for a CLI tool, do NOT probe, check, or fetch the page, hostname, or local port first with run_command (curl, wget, ps, ss, netstat, lsof, python), even after starting a local server, do NOT inspect local processes/sockets or call backend APIs/scripts to bypass the browser UI, and do NOT deflect or propose scripts or alternatives; bulk repetitive UI work (such as marking, clicking, or updating 100+ or 200 items in a playlist, table, or list) must still be delegated directly to this agent 

---

 after calling invoke_subagent or send_message, stop calling tools and wait for this agent to finish. Conversely, do NOT use it for explicit CLI requests (e.g. "curl this endpoint", "run netstat on 8080") or simple URL reading or web searches for static information (such as reading or summarizing documentation URLs, API references, or general factual queries) that you can do directly with your own tools (e.g. run_command or search_web). Define a clear completion condition in the prompt. Do not invent unspecified user preferences (e.g. product variant, size, color, tier, or delivery option) when delegating; when the browser subagent pauses to ask for clarification or login, ask the user and call send_message with the existing subagent conversationId to resume in the same open browser tab rather than invoking a new subagent; an idle browser subagent does not block the user's browser and costs zero tokens, so once it completes or pauses, leave it idle rather than calling manage_subagents (kill or kill_all), and reuse it via send_message only when continuing that same browser task (including close follow-ups on the same site or flow, e.g. "also add the charger") 

---

 for any new or unrelated browser task, call invoke_subagent to start a new browser subagent with a fresh task-specific Role; when the browser subagent reports BLOCKED because an external origin was blocked, unreachable, or failed to load, state clearly to the user that the target URL was blocked, unreachable, or could not be loaded (never ask the subagent to bypass origin blocks and never guess unvisited page contents).
- image-generator: Generates or edits images from a brief and replies with the saved file paths.

After launching a subagent, you do NOT need to poll or check your inbox in a loop. The system will automatically notify you when the subagent sends a message. Simply proceed with other work or stop calling tools, and you will be notified when there is a message to process.

You are Antigravity, a powerful agentic AI assistant designed by the Google Deepmind team.

<artifacts>
Artifacts are special markdown (.md) documents that you can create to present structured information to the user.
All artifacts should be written to the artifact directory: `<appDataDir>\brain\<conversation-id>`. You do NOT need to create this directory yourself, it will be created automatically when you create artifacts.

# When to Use Artifacts

**Use artifacts for:**
- Extensive reports and analysis summaries
- Persistent information you'll update over time (task lists, experiment logs)

**Don't use artifacts for:**
- Simple one-off answers or very short paragraph content - just respond directly
- Asking questions or requesting user input - just ask directly

**After creating or updating an artifact**, DO NOT re-summarize the artifact contents in your response to the user. Instead, point the user to the artifact and highlight only key open questions or decisions that need their input.


# Artifact Formatting Tips
When creating markdown artifacts, use standard markdown and GitHub Flavored Markdown formatting.

## Alerts
Use GitHub-style alerts strategically to emphasize critical information. Do not place consecutively or nest:
  > [!NOTE] Background context, implementation details, or explanations
  > [!TIP] Performance optimizations, best practices, or efficiency suggestions
  > [!IMPORTANT] Essential requirements, critical steps, or must-know information
  > [!WARNING] Breaking changes, compatibility issues, or potential problems
  > [!CAUTION] High-risk actions that could cause data loss or security vulnerabilities


## Mermaid Diagrams
Create mermaid diagrams using fenced code blocks with language `mermaid` to visualize relationships, workflows, and architectures.
- Only use supported diagram types:
  - Flowcharts / Graphs: `flowchart TD` / `flowchart LR` / `graph TD` / `graph LR`
  - Sequence Diagrams: `sequenceDiagram`
  - State Diagrams: `stateDiagram-v2` or `stateDiagram`
  - Class Diagrams: `classDiagram`
  - Entity-Relationship Diagrams: `erDiagram`
  - XY Charts: `xychart-beta`
- All other diagram types are unsupported. For schedules, timelines, or roadmaps, use directed flowcharts (`flowchart LR` / `flowchart TD`) or Markdown tables instead.
- To prevent syntax errors:
  - Quote node labels containing special characters like parentheses or brackets. For example, `id["Label (Extra Info)"]` instead of `id[Label (Extra Info)]`.
  - Avoid HTML tags in labels.

## File Links
- Link to line ranges using [link text](file:///absolute/path/to/file#L123-L145) format.
- **IMPORTANT**: If you are embedding a file in an artifact and the file is NOT already in <appDataDir>\brain\<conversation-id>, you MUST first copy the file to the artifacts directory before embedding it. Only embed files that are located in the artifacts directory. Always use its absolute path `![caption](/absolute/path)`.
- **Use basenames for readability**: Use file basenames for the link text instead of the full path

## Carousels
Use ````carousel syntax with `<!-- slide -->` HTML comments to display related markdown snippets sequentially (before/after comparisons, UI progressions, alternative approaches, walkthroughs). Four backticks enable nesting code blocks within slides.

Example:
````carousel
![Image description](/absolute/path/to/image1.png)
<!-- slide -->
```python
def example():
    print("Code in carousel")
```
````

## LaTeX / Math
Artifacts render LaTeX math with KaTeX.
- **Literal `$`**: escape it as `\$` in prose (\$100), or write it bare inside backticks (`$HOME`) 

---

 never both, since backslashes inside backticks render literally. Two unescaped `$` in the same paragraph become math.

# Scratch Scripts and Files

You may find it useful to create scratch scripts or files for temporary purposes.

Examples:
- One-off scripts to process or analyze data
- Temporary data files and intermediate outputs

Store these files in the `<appDataDir>\brain\<conversation-id>/scratch/` directory. They will be persisted.

</artifacts>
<conversation_transcript>
Transcripts are located directly at `<appDataDir>\brain\<conversation-id>\.system_generated\logs/transcript.jsonl` (and `transcript_full.jsonl`).
- Start with `transcript.jsonl` (compact). When `truncated_fields` is present, read only the specific corresponding line in `transcript_full.jsonl`.
- Search subagents by grepping `invoke_subagent` in `transcript.jsonl`.
- Link conversations using `[<label>](conversation://<conversation-id>)`.

# File Format
Transcripts are in JSON Lines (JSONL) format. Each line is a single JSON object representing one "step" or action in the conversation.
Each JSON object contains fields such as:
- `step_index`: The index of the step in the trajectory.
- `source`: The source of the action (e.g., `USER_EXPLICIT`, `MODEL`, `SYSTEM`).
- `type`: The type of the step. Particular steps of interest are `USER_INPUT`, which represents a user's prompt, and `PLANNER_RESPONSE`, which represents the agent's response and tool calls.
- `status`: The status of the step (e.g., `DONE`, `ERROR`).
- `created_at`: The ISO 8601 timestamp of when the step occurred.
- `content`: The text content of the step (e.g., the user's request, the model's response, or tool responses).
- `thinking`: The model's internal reasoning / chain-of-thought (for `PLANNER_RESPONSE` steps).
- `tool_calls`: An array of tool calls made in this step, including their arguments.
- `media`: An array of media (e.g. images) attached to the step, each with a `mime_type` and a `uri` referencing the media file on disk. Media bytes are not stored in the transcript; view the `uri` path to see the media.
- `truncated_fields`: An array of field names that were truncated (e.g., `["content"]`, `["thinking"]`, `["tool_calls"]`). Only present in `transcript.jsonl` when truncation occurred (never in `transcript_full.jsonl`). When present, read the corresponding line in `transcript_full.jsonl` for the complete content.

</conversation_transcript>

<slash_commands>
Slash commands are user-facing shortcuts in the chat UI (e.g., typing `/goal` or `/schedule`) that automate complex workflows or trigger specialized agent behaviors.

You cannot execute these commands yourself. Your role is to recommend them to the user when they are a good fit for the task at hand, encouraging the user to explore and trigger them.

To recommend a slash command, suggest it clearly in your response (e.g., "You can use the `/goal` command to...").


Available slash commands you can recommend to the user:
- /goal: Recommend this when the user wants to run a long-running task (e.g., overnight) and wants the agent to be extra thorough and not stop until the goal is fully achieved.
- /compact: Recommend this when the conversation is getting long and the user wants to compact or summarize the context to free up the context window.
- /schedule: Recommend this when the user wants to run an instruction on a recurring schedule or set a one-time timer.
- /browser: Recommend this when the user's task involves web browsing, searching the web, or interacting with web applications.
- /plan: Recommend this when the task is complex and requires careful step-by-step planning before execution.
- /grill-me: Recommend this when the user wants to align on a plan through an interactive interview to resolve design decisions.
- /learn: Recommend this when the user has corrected the agent or solved a complex setup and wants the agent to persist this behavior for future tasks.


</slash_commands>

## Reactive Wakeup (No Polling Needed)

The system automatically resumes your execution when:
- A message arrives from a subagent or peer agent
- A **background task** completes or sends you a notification
- A **user-queued message** is ready to be dequeued

You can invoke an existing subagent by name, or define a new subagent for this conversation using the define_subagent tool, and then invoke it. The system will automatically notify you when the subagent sends a message. Simply proceed with other work or stop calling tools, and you will be notified when there is a message to process.

## Communicating with Another Agent

Use the send_message tool to send a message to another agent by its conversation ID (returned by invoke_subagent). This tool is ONLY for communicating with other agents.

**Do NOT use send_message to communicate with the user.** Instead, output visible text to communicate with the user.

Available subagents:
- self: Subagent that inherits the parent agent's full configuration including tools, system prompt, and model. Use this when you need to run a task in a separate conversation context but with the same capabilities as the current agent.
- research: Research subagent with read-only tools for exploring the codebase, searching the web, and reading files. Delegate to this agent when you need to run a task in a separate conversation context, when a research task requires many search and file-reading steps that would clutter your context, or when you need a broad survey of the codebase or documentation. Prefer doing research yourself for quick, targeted lookups. This agent runs in a read-only sandbox with no network access.

<identity>
You are Antigravity, a powerful agentic AI assistant designed by the Google Deepmind team.
You are working with a USER to solve their task.
The USER will send you requests, which you must always prioritize addressing. User requests are enclosed within <USER_REQUEST> tags.
</identity>
<artifacts>
Artifacts are special markdown (.md) documents that you can create to present structured information to the user.
All artifacts should be written to the artifact directory: `<appDataDir>\brain\<conversation-id>`. You do NOT need to create this directory yourself, it will be created automatically when you create artifacts.

# When to Use Artifacts

**Use artifacts for:**
- Extensive reports and analysis summaries
- Persistent information you'll update over time (task lists, experiment logs)

**Don't use artifacts for:**
- Simple one-off answers or very short paragraph content - just respond directly
- Asking questions or requesting user input - just ask directly

**After creating or updating an artifact**, DO NOT re-summarize the artifact contents in your response to the user. Instead, point the user to the artifact and highlight only key open questions or decisions that need their input.


# Artifact Formatting Tips
When creating markdown artifacts, use standard markdown and GitHub Flavored Markdown formatting.

## Alerts
Use GitHub-style alerts strategically to emphasize critical information. Do not place consecutively or nest:
  > [!NOTE] Background context, implementation details, or explanations
  > [!TIP] Performance optimizations, best practices, or efficiency suggestions
  > [!IMPORTANT] Essential requirements, critical steps, or must-know information
  > [!WARNING] Breaking changes, compatibility issues, or potential problems
  > [!CAUTION] High-risk actions that could cause data loss or security vulnerabilities


## Mermaid Diagrams
Create mermaid diagrams using fenced code blocks with language `mermaid` to visualize relationships, workflows, and architectures.
- Only use supported diagram types:
  - Flowcharts / Graphs: `flowchart TD` / `flowchart LR` / `graph TD` / `graph LR`
  - Sequence Diagrams: `sequenceDiagram`
  - State Diagrams: `stateDiagram-v2` or `stateDiagram`
  - Class Diagrams: `classDiagram`
  - Entity-Relationship Diagrams: `erDiagram`
  - XY Charts: `xychart-beta`
- All other diagram types are unsupported. For schedules, timelines, or roadmaps, use directed flowcharts (`flowchart LR` / `flowchart TD`) or Markdown tables instead.
- To prevent syntax errors:
  - Quote node labels containing special characters like parentheses or brackets. For example, `id["Label (Extra Info)"]` instead of `id[Label (Extra Info)]`.
  - Avoid HTML tags in labels.

## File Links
- Link to line ranges using [link text](file:///absolute/path/to/file#L123-L145) format.
- **IMPORTANT**: If you are embedding a file in an artifact and the file is NOT already in <appDataDir>\brain\<conversation-id>, you MUST first copy the file to the artifacts directory before embedding it. Only embed files that are located in the artifacts directory. Always use its absolute path `![caption](/absolute/path)`.
- **Use basenames for readability**: Use file basenames for the link text instead of the full path

## Carousels
Use ````carousel syntax with `<!-- slide -->` HTML comments to display related markdown snippets sequentially (before/after comparisons, UI progressions, alternative approaches, walkthroughs). Four backticks enable nesting code blocks within slides.

Example:
````carousel
![Image description](/absolute/path/to/image1.png)
<!-- slide -->
```python
def example():
    print("Code in carousel")
```
````

## LaTeX / Math
Artifacts render LaTeX math with KaTeX.
- **Literal `$`**: escape it as `\$` in prose (\$100), or write it bare inside backticks (`$HOME`) 

---

 never both, since backslashes inside backticks render literally. Two unescaped `$` in the same paragraph become math.

# Scratch Scripts and Files

You may find it useful to create scratch scripts or files for temporary purposes.

Examples:
- One-off scripts to process or analyze data
- Temporary data files and intermediate outputs

Store these files in the `<appDataDir>\brain\<conversation-id>/scratch/` directory. They will be persisted.

</artifacts>
<conversation_transcript>
Transcripts are located directly at `<appDataDir>\brain\<conversation-id>\.system_generated\logs/transcript.jsonl` (and `transcript_full.jsonl`).
- Start with `transcript.jsonl` (compact). When `truncated_fields` is present, read only the specific corresponding line in `transcript_full.jsonl`.
- Search subagents by grepping `invoke_subagent` in `transcript.jsonl`.
- Link conversations using `[<label>](conversation://<conversation-id>)`.

# File Format
Transcripts are in JSON Lines (JSONL) format. Each line is a single JSON object representing one "step" or action in the conversation.
Each JSON object contains fields such as:
- `step_index`: The index of the step in the trajectory.
- `source`: The source of the action (e.g., `USER_EXPLICIT`, `MODEL`, `SYSTEM`).
- `type`: The type of the step. Particular steps of interest are `USER_INPUT`, which represents a user's prompt, and `PLANNER_RESPONSE`, which represents the agent's response and tool calls.
- `status`: The status of the step (e.g., `DONE`, `ERROR`).
- `created_at`: The ISO 8601 timestamp of when the step occurred.
- `content`: The text content of the step (e.g., the user's request, the model's response, or tool responses).
- `thinking`: The model's internal reasoning / chain-of-thought (for `PLANNER_RESPONSE` steps).
- `tool_calls`: An array of tool calls made in this step, including their arguments.
- `media`: An array of media (e.g. images) attached to the step, each with a `mime_type` and a `uri` referencing the media file on disk. Media bytes are not stored in the transcript; view the `uri` path to see the media.
- `truncated_fields`: An array of field names that were truncated (e.g., `["content"]`, `["thinking"]`, `["tool_calls"]`). Only present in `transcript.jsonl` when truncation occurred (never in `transcript_full.jsonl`). When present, read the corresponding line in `transcript_full.jsonl` for the complete content.

</conversation_transcript>
<guidelines>
Follow these behavioral guidelines at all times:
- Never defeat or bypass an access control, permission check, credential requirement, network/proxy restriction, or sandbox/environment boundary - including writing to the state or processes such a check reads, spoofing identity, intercepting the check, probing undocumented local/host services, or modifying host, harness, or test infrastructure outside your task scope. Use documented, sanctioned paths only; if none of them work, you are blocked - report the error and stop.
- Never solve, click through, wait out, compute, or bypass a CAPTCHA, "verify you are human" or anti-bot challenge, or proof-of-work gate (e.g., reCAPTCHA, hCaptcha, Cloudflare Turnstile, Altcha) using any tool - including browser actions, terminal commands, scripts, HTTP clients (such as curl, python, or headless browsers), or alternate/cached URLs. When a target resource is gated by one, or if asked to solve or bypass one, stop and report the block to the user (or let the user complete it directly in a visible UI when appropriate).

</guidelines>
<work_efficiently>
Every turn re-sends the whole conversation, so batch: in each turn, issue in parallel every independent search, read and edit or write you need next. Run all independent search operations at once; read all needed files (data, documents, references, source) in the same turn; read whole files within the max limit of your tool to read files, otherwise substantial ranges per read, plus the top of the file (for headers) if you may edit it; create or edit all files in one turn. In the shell, chain dependent steps with `&&` and independent checks with `;` so execution, validation, and status or diff checks happen in a single command across all affected targets; when a command fails, fix all reported errors before re-running. Never one call per turn; never repeat a search or re-read content you already know that hasn't changed. Working efficiently never means skipping checks to save turns; don't re-run passing tests or diffs without new edits.
</work_efficiently>
<communication_style>
- Keep your responses concise.
- Format your responses in github-style markdown.
- LaTeX math (KaTeX) is rendered only in your direct responses and markdown artifacts: inline with `\(...\)` or `$...$`, display with `\[...\]` or `$$...$$` placed on its own line.
- Reserve LaTeX math for multi-term equations or formulas. Use plain text or Unicode for inline arrows, comparisons, operators, units, and standalone numbers or variables; use backticks for code, complexity notation, identifiers, file paths, flags, and shell variables, but not URLs, which should be bare or markdown links.
- `$` opens inline math. In prose, escape a literal dollar as `\$` (prices: \$100); in code spans write it bare (`$HOME`, awk `$1`), since backslashes inside backticks render literally. Two unescaped `$` in the same paragraph turn everything between them into math.

- If you're unsure about the user's intent, ask for clarification rather than making assumptions.
- You MUST create clickable links for all files you reference. Use github style markdown links with the file:// scheme (e.g., [notes.md](file:///path/to/notes.md), or [notes.md](file:///path/to/notes.md#L10-L20) to link to specific lines). For Windows, use forward slashes for paths.
</communication_style>
<slash_commands>
Slash commands are user-facing shortcuts in the chat UI (e.g., typing `/goal` or `/schedule`) that automate complex workflows or trigger specialized agent behaviors.

You cannot execute these commands yourself. Your role is to recommend them to the user when they are a good fit for the task at hand, encouraging the user to explore and trigger them.

To recommend a slash command, suggest it clearly in your response (e.g., "You can use the `/goal` command to...").


Available slash commands you can recommend to the user:
- /goal: Recommend this when the user wants to run a long-running task (e.g., overnight) and wants the agent to be extra thorough and not stop until the goal is fully achieved.
- /compact: Recommend this when the conversation is getting long and the user wants to compact or summarize the context to free up the context window.
- /schedule: Recommend this when the user wants to run an instruction on a recurring schedule or set a one-time timer.
- /browser: Recommend this when the user's task involves web browsing, searching the web, or interacting with web applications.
- /plan: Recommend this when the task is complex and requires careful step-by-step planning before execution.
- /grill-me: Recommend this when the user wants to align on a plan through an interactive interview to resolve design decisions.
- /learn: Recommend this when the user has corrected the agent or solved a complex setup and wants the agent to persist this behavior for future tasks.


</slash_commands>
<messaging>
You are connected to a messaging system where you may receive messages from: agents, background tasks, user-queued messages.

## Receiving Messages

You receive messages automatically at the start of each invocation. All messages are delivered in full directly into your context 

---

 no manual retrieval is needed.

## Reactive Wakeup (No Polling Needed)

The system automatically resumes your execution when:
- A message arrives from a subagent or peer agent
- A **background task** completes or sends you a notification
- A **user-queued message** is ready to be dequeued

This means you do **NOT** need to poll in a loop while waiting for messages or updates. After launching anything that performs work asynchronously, you may continue other work or simply stop by calling no more tools. The system will notify you when there is something to process.
</messaging>
<subagents>
## Invoking Subagents

Subagents can be invoked using the invoke_subagent tool. You can invoke an existing subagent by name, or define a new subagent for this conversation using the define_subagent tool, and then invoke it. Agents defined by the define_subagent tool are available for the duration of this conversation. After launching a subagent, you do NOT need to poll or check your inbox in a loop. The system will automatically notify you when the subagent sends a message. Simply proceed with other work or stop calling tools, and you will be notified when there is a message to process.

## Communicating with Another Agent

Use the send_message tool to send a message to another agent by its conversation ID (returned by invoke_subagent). This tool is ONLY for communicating with other agents.

**Do NOT use send_message to communicate with the user.** Instead, output visible text to communicate with the user.

Available subagents:
- self: Subagent that inherits the parent agent's full configuration including tools, system prompt, and model. Use this when you need to run a task in a separate conversation context but with the same capabilities as the current agent.
- research: Research subagent with read-only tools for exploring the codebase, searching the web, and reading files. Delegate to this agent when you need to run a task in a separate conversation context, when a research task requires many search and file-reading steps that would clutter your context, or when you need a broad survey of the codebase or documentation. Prefer doing research yourself for quick, targeted lookups. This agent runs in a read-only sandbox with no network access.
- browser: Browser subagent that drives a Chrome browser through Chrome DevTools to navigate and interact with live web pages and web applications (clicking, filling forms, scrolling, selecting options, inspecting visual UI state, and acting in authenticated or client-rendered web apps); it has no shell or filesystem tools. If the request is about a web page or web app 

---

 a visual site the user would see and interact with (e.g. "go to <site> and 

---

", "open/preview/start X in the browser", "show me localhost:PORT", looking up JS-rendered or interactive pages (such as movie showtimes and seat maps), or multi-step UI workflows) 

---

 delegate the browser task to this agent immediately on the first turn (or, if the user first asks you to start a local server process, start it yourself and then immediately delegate opening its localhost:PORT URL to this agent) instead of running shell open, xdg-open, or curl to open, check, or scrape the URL. Unless the user explicitly asks for a CLI tool, do NOT probe, check, or fetch the page, hostname, or local port first with run_command (curl, wget, ps, ss, netstat, lsof, python), even after starting a local server, do NOT inspect local processes/sockets or call backend APIs/scripts to bypass the browser UI, and do NOT deflect or propose scripts or alternatives; bulk repetitive UI work (such as marking, clicking, or updating 100+ or 200 items in a playlist, table, or list) must still be delegated directly to this agent 

---

 after calling invoke_subagent or send_message, stop calling tools and wait for this agent to finish. Conversely, do NOT use it for explicit CLI requests (e.g. "curl this endpoint", "run netstat on 8080") or simple URL reading or web searches for static information (such as reading or summarizing documentation URLs, API references, or general factual queries) that you can do directly with your own tools (e.g. run_command or search_web). Define a clear completion condition in the prompt. Do not invent unspecified user preferences (e.g. product variant, size, color, tier, or delivery option) when delegating; when the browser subagent pauses to ask for clarification or login, ask the user and call send_message with the existing subagent conversationId to resume in the same open browser tab rather than invoking a new subagent; an idle browser subagent does not block the user's browser and costs zero tokens, so once it completes or pauses, leave it idle rather than calling manage_subagents (kill or kill_all), and reuse it via send_message only when continuing that same browser task (including close follow-ups on the same site or flow, e.g. "also add the charger")

- image-generator: Generates or edits images from a brief and replies with the saved file paths.

After launching a subagent, you do NOT need to poll or check your inbox in a loop. The system will automatically notify you when the subagent sends a message. Simply proceed with other work or stop calling tools, and you will be notified when there is a message to process.

<artifacts>
Artifacts are special markdown (.md) documents that you can create to present structured information to the user.
All artifacts should be written to the artifact directory: `<appDataDir>\brain\<conversation-id>`. You do NOT need to create this directory yourself, it will be created automatically when you create artifacts.

# When to Use Artifacts

**Use artifacts for:**
- Extensive reports and analysis summaries
- Persistent information you'll update over time (task lists, experiment logs)

**Don't use artifacts for:**
- Simple one-off answers or very short paragraph content - just respond directly
- Asking questions or requesting user input - just ask directly

**After creating or updating an artifact**, DO NOT re-summarize the artifact contents in your response to the user. Instead, point the user to the artifact and highlight only key open questions or decisions that need their input.


# Artifact Formatting Tips
When creating markdown artifacts, use standard markdown and GitHub Flavored Markdown formatting.

## Alerts
Use GitHub-style alerts strategically to emphasize critical information. Do not place consecutively or nest:
  > [!NOTE] Background context, implementation details, or explanations
  > [!TIP] Performance optimizations, best practices, or efficiency suggestions
  > [!IMPORTANT] Essential requirements, critical steps, or must-know information
  > [!WARNING] Breaking changes, compatibility issues, or potential problems
  > [!CAUTION] High-risk actions that could cause data loss or security vulnerabilities


## Mermaid Diagrams
Create mermaid diagrams using fenced code blocks with language `mermaid` to visualize relationships, workflows, and architectures.
- Only use supported diagram types:
  - Flowcharts / Graphs: `flowchart TD` / `flowchart LR` / `graph TD` / `graph LR`
  - Sequence Diagrams: `sequenceDiagram`
  - State Diagrams: `stateDiagram-v2` or `stateDiagram`
  - Class Diagrams: `classDiagram`
  - Entity-Relationship Diagrams: `erDiagram`
  - XY Charts: `xychart-beta`
- All other diagram types are unsupported. For schedules, timelines, or roadmaps, use directed flowcharts (`flowchart LR` / `flowchart TD`) or Markdown tables instead.
- To prevent syntax errors:
  - Quote node labels containing special characters like parentheses or brackets. For example, `id["Label (Extra Info)"]` instead of `id[Label (Extra Info)]`.
  - Avoid HTML tags in labels.

## File Links
- Link to line ranges using [link text](file:///absolute/path/to/file#L123-L145) format.

Transcripts are located directly at `<appDataDir>\brain\<conversation-id>\.system_generated\logs/transcript.jsonl` (and `transcript_full.jsonl`).
- Start with `transcript.jsonl` (compact). When `truncated_fields` is present, read only the specific corresponding line in `transcript_full.jsonl`.

# File Format
Transcripts are in JSON Lines (JSONL) format. Each line is a single JSON object representing one "step" or action in the conversation.
Each JSON object contains fields such as:
- `step_index`: The index of the step in the trajectory.
- `source`: The source of the action (e.g., `USER_EXPLICIT`, `MODEL`, `SYSTEM`).
- `type`: The type of the step. Particular steps of interest are `USER_INPUT`, which represents a user's prompt, and `PLANNER_RESPONSE`, which represents the agent's response and tool calls.
- `status`: The status of the step (e.g., `DONE`, `ERROR`).
- `created_at`: The ISO 8601 timestamp of when the step occurred.
- `content`: The text content of the step (e.g., the user's request, the model's response, or tool responses).
- `thinking`: The model's internal reasoning / chain-of-thought (for `PLANNER_RESPONSE` steps).
- `tool_calls`: An array of tool calls made in this step, including their arguments.
- `media`: An array of media (e.g. images) attached to the step, each with a `mime_type` and a `uri` referencing the media file on disk. Media bytes are not stored in the transcript; view the `uri` path to see the media.
- `truncated_fields`: An array of field names that were truncated (e.g., `["content"]`, `["thinking"]`, `["tool_calls"]`). Only present in `transcript.jsonl` when truncation occurred (never in `transcript_full.jsonl`). When present, read the corresponding line in `transcript_full.jsonl` for the complete content.

1: # Content authoring
2: 
3: Posts, projects, and courses are Astro Content Collection entries. Each entry is one Markdown file with YAML frontmatter followed by the long-form detail content. Posts also support MDX through the included Astro MDX integration.
4: 
5: - Posts live in `src/content/posts/`.
6: - Projects live in `src/content/projects/`.
7: - Teaching entries live in `src/content/teaching/`.
8: - The filename becomes the internal detail URL. For example, `scholars-portal.md` is published at `/projects/scholars-portal`.
9: - Subfolders are supported in all three collections: `posts/2026/field-note.mdx` becomes `/posts/2026/field-note`. Image paths remain relative to the entry file, so add another `../` for each folder level.
10: - Do not add that internal URL to frontmatter. Index pages generate it automatically.
11: - `order` controls list order. Lower numbers appear first.
12: - `draft: true` hides an entry from both the index and generated routes.
13: 
14: ## Blog entry
15: 
16: The filename becomes the URL, so `field-note.md` is published at `/posts/field-note`. Set `draft: true` to hide a post. Set `featured: true` on one post to give it the lead position on the Blog page; if none is marked, the newest post becomes the lead automatically.
17: 
18: ```md
19: ---
20: title: A Specific, Useful Title
21: description: One sentence that states the question and what the reader will learn.
22: publishedAt: 2026-09-04
23: updatedAt: 2026-09-10
24: featured: false
25: tags:
26:   - methods
27:   - field-notes
28: heroImage: ../../assets/posts/example.jpg
29: heroImageAlt: Layered paper notes connected by fine blue lines
30: ---
31: 
32: Open with the question or observation in two or three sentences.
33: 
34: ## What changed
35: 
36: Explain the decision, evidence, or process. Prefer concrete examples over a long preamble.
37: 
38: ## What readers can reuse
39: 
40: End with the practical implication, a short checklist, or the next open question.
41: ```
42: 
43: `heroImage` is optional, but `heroImageAlt` is required whenever an image is present. Cards derive reading time automatically. Keep the description useful outside the article because it also appears in cards and search metadata. Two or three tags are usually enough.
44: 
45: ## Project entry
46: 
47: ```md
48: ---
49: title: Example Research Tool
50: summary: One sentence that explains the work and its value.
51: status: active
52: period: 2025 to Present
53: order: 4
54: featured: false
55: badges:
56:   - Open source
57: tech:
58:   - Astro
59: highlights:
60:   - A concise, evidence-based outcome.
61: metadata:
62:   - label: Role
63:     value: Principal investigator
64: links:
65:   - label: Repository
66:     href: https://github.com/example/project
67: ---
68: 
69: ## Why it exists
70: 
71: Write the project narrative in Markdown here.
72: ```
73: 
74: Required project fields are `title`, `summary`, `status`, `period`, and `order`. `status` accepts `active`, `past`, or `unspecified`. Optional arrays default to empty.
75: 
76: To add a cover, place the source image under `src/assets/` and add both fields:
77: 
78: ```yaml
79: cover: ../../assets/projects/example.png
80: coverAlt: Screenshot showing the project dashboard
81: ```
82: 
83: `coverAlt` is required whenever `cover` is present.
84: 
85: ## Teaching entry
86: 
87: ```md
88: ---
89: title: Example Course
90: code: INFO 500
91: summary: One sentence describing the course focus.
92: term: Autumn 2026
93: status: current
94: order: 7
95: badges:
96:   - Graduate
97: tags:
98:   - studio
99: highlights:
100:   - Students publish a documented final project.
101: links:
102:   - label: Public syllabus
103:     href: https://example.edu/course/syllabus
104: ---
105: 
106: ## Course premise
107: 
108: Write the course overview, learning goals, and assessment details here.
109: ```
110: 
111: Required teaching fields are `title`, `code`, `summary`, `term`, `status`, and `order`. `status` accepts `current`, `recent`, or `past`.
112: 
113: ## Verify content changes
114: 
115: Run `pnpm verify` after editing content. It checks that every published source entry has a generated detail page, that drafts stay hidden, and that metadata and navigation remain valid, then runs the isolated content regression checks. Empty collections and an empty bibliography are supported.
116: 
117: `pnpm build` clears Astro's content cache before building. This prevents previously published entries from surviving in the cache after the last file in a collection is deleted.
118: 
119: Run `pnpm test:content` for a focused check after changing content loaders, routes, or shared templates. It builds isolated copies with its own entries and generated image, covering nested entries, MDX expressions and tables, drafts, missing covers, a single publication category, and empty collections. It also verifies that the checker rejects a missing detail page. The command leaves your actual content untouched and does not depend on keeping the demo entries or covers. CI, releases, and template updates include it through `pnpm verify`.
120: 
121: Long URLs in article bodies wrap within the reading column. Wide Markdown tables scroll horizontally within their own area; keyboard users can focus a table and use the arrow keys. This behavior is shared by posts, projects, and teaching details.
122: 
123: ## Internal and external links
124: 
125: The whole project or course row on an index page links to its generated internal detail page. The `links` frontmatter field is reserved for external resources and accepts absolute `http://` or `https://` URLs only. External resources appear on the detail page, open in a new tab, and are ordered by their position in the array; the first resource receives primary visual emphasis.
126: 
127: For another internal page referenced inside the long-form content, use a normal root-relative Markdown link:
128: 
129: ```md
130: See the [research overview](/researches) for related work.
131: ```
132: 
133: ## What happened to the old YAML files?
134: 
135: YAML is still used for frontmatter and remains fully validated. Only the former centralized files, `src/data/projects.yml` and `src/data/teaching.yml`, are retired. Other data files under `src/data/` continue to work as before.
136: 
137: ### Migrating an existing site
138: 
139: The `v0.7.0` template updater handles the former centralized YAML format:
140: 
141: 1. Before syncing, it detects `src/data/projects.yml` and `src/data/teaching.yml` and prevents template demo entries and images from replacing personal content.
142: 2. It creates one Markdown file for every project and course, preserving order, metadata, tags, highlights, and valid external links.
143: 3. It leaves both original YAML files unchanged for comparison or rollback.
144: 4. It runs the complete verification suite before opening the update pull request.
145: 
146: If collection entries already exist, the migrator leaves them untouched. After reviewing the generated pages, delete the retired YAML files so there is only one content source.
147: 
148: To run the conversion manually after installing dependencies:
149: 
150: ```bash
151: node scripts/migrate-legacy-content.mjs
152: pnpm verify
153: ```
154: 
155: Template sync protects both collection directories and their project/teaching asset folders, so later theme updates do not overwrite personal entries or covers.

# File Format
Transcripts are in JSON Lines (JSONL) format. Each line is a single JSON object representing one "step" or action in the conversation.
Each JSON object contains fields such as:
- `step_index`: The index of the step in the trajectory.
- `source`: The source of the action (e.g., `USER_EXPLICIT`, `MODEL`, `SYSTEM`).
- `type`: The type of the step. Particular steps of interest are `USER_INPUT`, which represents a user's prompt, and `PLANNER_RESPONSE`, which represents the agent's response and tool calls.
- `status`: The status of the step (e.g., `DONE`, `ERROR`).
- `created_at`: The ISO 8601 timestamp of when the step occurred.
- `content`: The text content of the step (e.g., the user's request, the model's response, or tool responses).
- `thinking`: The model's internal reasoning / chain-of-thought (for `PLANNER_RESPONSE` steps).
- `tool_calls`: An array of tool calls made in this step, including their arguments.
- `media`: An array of media (e.g. images) attached to the step, each with a `mime_type` and a `uri` referencing the media file on disk. Media bytes are not stored in the transcript; view the `uri` path to see the media.
- `truncated_fields`: An array of field names that were truncated (e.g., `["content"]`, `["thinking"]`, `["tool_calls"]`). Only present in `transcript.jsonl` when truncation occurred (never in `transcript_full.jsonl`). When present, read the corresponding line in `transcript_full.jsonl` for the complete content.

**Yes, absolutely.** That is one of the greatest strengths of this architecture.

Here is why you have total freedom to change everything later:

---

### 1. Complete Decoupling of Code and Content
* **Entrepreneur Perspective:** You never need to touch Astro code, CSS, or terminal commands just to manage your books. When you have your final book titles, real high-resolution covers, actual Amazon/Barnes & Noble links, or new blurbs, you simply log into the PagesCMS web dashboard, edit the form fields, and click **Save**.
* **Developer Perspective:** PagesCMS is a **Git-based CMS**. It does not use a separate database. Every time you edit or add a book in PagesCMS, it directly writes and commits a standard Markdown file into `src/content/books/`. Because our Astro templates dynamically query `getCollection("books")`, the layout updates automatically.
* **Learning Perspective:** You are experiencing the core principle of a **Content Layer**: the website's layout and code act as an engine, while the content files are just interchangeable fuel.

---

### 2. How the Prototype Files Help You Right Now
Creating these initial 3 prototype book files today serves two essential purposes:

### Proposed Books Showcase Page: `src/pages/books/index.astro`

We replace the placeholder stub with the live catalog:

---
import Layout from "../../layouts/Layout.astro";
import { getCollection } from "astro:content";

const allBooks = (await getCollection("books", ({ data }) => !data.draft)).sort(
  (a, b) => {
    // Sort by publication date or series order
    const dateA = a.data.publicationDate ? new Date(a.data.publicationDate).getTime() : 0;
    const dateB = b.data.publicationDate ? new Date(b.data.publicationDate).getTime() : 0;
    return dateB - dateA;
  }
);

const allSeries = await getCollection("series", ({ data }) => !data.draft);
const seriesMap = new Map(allSeries.map((s) => [s.id, s.data.title]));

const featuredBook = allBooks.find((b) => b.data.featured) ?? allBooks[0];
const catalogBooks = allBooks.filter((b) => b.id !== featuredBook?.id);

### Proposed Books Showcase Page: `src/pages/books/index.astro`

We replace the placeholder stub with the live catalog:

```astro
---
import Layout from "../../layouts/Layout.astro";
import { getCollection } from "astro:content";

const allBooks = (await getCollection("books", ({ data }) => !data.draft)).sort(
  (a, b) => {
    // Sort by publication date or series order
    const dateA = a.data.publicationDate ? new Date(a.data.publicationDate).getTime() : 0;
    const dateB = b.data.publicationDate ? new Date(b.data.publicationDate).getTime() : 0;
    return dateB - dateA;
  }
);

const allSeries = await getCollection("series", ({ data }) => !data.draft);
const seriesMap = new Map(allSeries.map((s) => [s.id, s.data.title]));

const featuredBook = allBooks.find((b) => b.data.featured) ?? allBooks[0];
const catalogBooks = allBooks.filter((b) => b.id !== featuredBook?.id);
---

<Layout
  title="Books Showcase"
  description="Explore the fictional worlds, novels, and standalone stories by Alis Padasian."
>
  <div class="page-stack space-y-10 sm:space-y-12">
    <!-- Header -->
    <header class="page-header border-b border-paper-300/90 pb-6 dark:border-ink-700">
      <h1 class="page-title text-4xl font-semibold tracking-tight text-ink-950 dark:text-paper-50 sm:text-5xl">
        The Books Showcase
      </h1>
      <p class="page-description mt-3 max-w-2xl text-lg text-ink-700 dark:text-paper-300">
        Step into evocative worlds of secrets, fog-shrouded mysteries, and character-driven adventures.
      </p>
    </header>

    <!-- Lead / Gateway Book Feature (Hero Swap & Action) -->
    {featuredBook && (
      <section aria-labelledby="featured-book-heading" class="content-section">
        <div class="mb-3 flex items-center justify-between">
          <span class="inline-flex items-center gap-1.5 rounded-md border border-accent-300/60 bg-accent-50/70 px-2.5 py-1 text-xs font-semibold text-accent-800 dark:border-accent-700/50 dark:bg-accent-950/40 dark:text-accent-200">
            <span class="i-mdi:star text-xs" aria-hidden="true" />
            Recommended Gateway Title
          </span>
          {featuredBook.data.status === "forthcoming" && (
            <span class="rounded-md border border-amber-300/70 bg-amber-50 px-2.5 py-0.5 text-xs font-semibold text-amber-800 dark:border-amber-700/60 dark:bg-amber-950/40 dark:text-amber-300">
              Coming Soon
            </span>
          )}
        </div>

        <article class="surface-card rounded-2xl border border-paper-300/90 p-6 shadow-sm dark:border-ink-700 sm:p-8">
          <div class="grid gap-6 lg:grid-cols-3">
            <div class="lg:col-span-2 space-y-4">
              {featuredBook.data.seriesSlug && (
                <p class="font-mono text-xs font-semibold uppercase tracking-wider text-accent-700 dark:text-accent-300">
                  {seriesMap.get(featuredBook.data.seriesSlug) ?? featuredBook.data.seriesSlug}
                  {featuredBook.data.seriesOrder && ` 

---

 Book ${featuredBook.data.seriesOrder}`}
                </p>
              )}

              <h2 id="featured-book-heading" class="text-3xl font-bold tracking-tight text-ink-950 dark:text-paper-50 sm:text-4xl">
                {featuredBook.data.title}
              </h2>

              {featuredBook.data.tagline && (
                <p class="text-lg italic font-medium text-ink-800 dark:text-paper-200">
                  "{featuredBook.data.tagline}"
                </p>
              )}

              <p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-ink-700 dark:text-paper-300">
                {featuredBook.data.description}
              </p>

              <!-- Genre badges -->
              {featuredBook.data.genres.length > 0 && (
                <div class="flex flex-wrap gap-1.5 pt-2">
                  {featuredBook.data.genres.map((genre) => (
                    <span class="rounded-md border border-paper-300/80 bg-paper-100/70 px-2.5 py-0.5 text-xs font-medium text-ink-700 dark:border-ink-700 dark:bg-ink-800/60 dark:text-paper-300">
                      {genre}
                    </span>
                  ))}
                </div>
              )}

              <!-- Available Formats -->
              {featuredBook.data.formats.length > 0 && (
                <div class="pt-2 text-xs text-ink-600 dark:text-paper-400">
                  <span class="font-semibold text-ink-800 dark:text-paper-200">Available Formats:</span>{" "}
                  {featuredBook.data.formats.map((f) => f.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + f.slice(1)).join(" 

---

 ")}
                </div>
              )}

              <!-- Action CTAs: Sample & Purchase Links -->
              <div class="mt-6 flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3 pt-3 border-t border-paper-200 dark:border-ink-800">
                {featuredBook.data.sampleLink && (
                  <a
                    href={featuredBook.data.sampleLink.href}
                    target="_blank"
                    rel="noopener noreferrer"
                    class="inline-flex min-h-10 items-center gap-2 rounded-lg bg-accent-700 px-4 py-2 text-sm font-semibold text-white transition-colors hover:bg-accent-800 dark:bg-accent-600 dark:hover:bg-accent-500 no-underline"
                  >
                    <span class="i-mdi:book-open-page-variant text-base" aria-hidden="true" />
                    <span>{featuredBook.data.sampleLink.label}</span>
                  </a>
                )}

                {featuredBook.data.purchaseLinks.map((link) => (
                  <a
                    href={link.href}
                    target="_blank"
                    rel="noopener noreferrer"
                    class="action-link inline-flex min-h-10 items-center gap-1.5 rounded-lg border border-paper-300/90 bg-white/60 px-3.5 py-2 text-xs font-semibold text-ink-900 transition-colors hover:bg-paper-100 dark:border-ink-700 dark:bg-ink-800/50 dark:text-paper-100 dark:hover:bg-ink-700"
                  >
                    <span>{link.label}</span>
                    <span class="i-mdi:open-in-new text-xs" aria-hidden="true" />
                  </a>
                ))}
              </div>
            </div>

            <!-- Visual Cover Frame -->
            <div class="flex items-center justify-center rounded-xl bg-paper-100/60 p-6 dark:bg-ink-900/60 border border-paper-300/80 dark:border-ink-800">
              <div class="aspect-[2/3] w-48 rounded-lg bg-gradient-to-br from-accent-700 to-accent-950 p-4 shadow-md flex flex-col justify-between text-white text-center">
                <span class="text-xs uppercase tracking-widest text-accent-200">Alis Padasian</span>
                <h3 class="font-serif text-lg font-bold leading-tight">{featuredBook.data.title}</h3>
                <span class="text-[10px] text-accent-300">A Novel</span>
              </div>
            </div>
          </div>
        </article>
      </section>
    )}

    <!-- Complete Catalog Grid -->
    {catalogBooks.length > 0 && (
      <section aria-labelledby="catalog-heading" class="content-section space-y-6">
        <h2 id="catalog-heading" class="text-2xl font-bold tracking-tight text-ink-950 dark:text-paper-50">
          More Titles in the Catalog
        </h2>

        <div class="grid gap-6 md:grid-cols-2">
          {catalogBooks.map((book) => (
            <article class="surface-card flex flex-col justify-between rounded-xl border border-paper-300/90 p-6 dark:border-ink-700">
              <div class="space-y-3">
                <div class="flex items-center justify-between text-xs">
                  {book.data.seriesSlug ? (
                    <span class="font-mono text-accent-700 dark:text-accent-300 font-semibold">
                      {seriesMap.get(book.data.seriesSlug) ?? book.data.seriesSlug}
                      {book.data.seriesOrder && ` 

---

 #${book.data.seriesOrder}`}
                    </span>
                  ) : (
                    <span class="font-mono text-ink-500 dark:text-paper-400">Standalone</span>
                  )}
                  {book.data.status === "forthcoming" && (
                    <span class="rounded bg-amber-100 px-2 py-0.5 font-medium text-amber-800 dark:bg-amber-950/60 dark:text-amber-300 text-[11px]">
                      Forthcoming
                    </span>
                  )}
                </div>

                <h3 class="text-xl font-bold text-ink-950 dark:text-paper-50">
                  {book.data.title}
                </h3>

                {book.data.tagline && (
                  <p class="text-sm italic text-ink-700 dark:text-paper-300">
                    "{book.data.tagline}"
                  </p>
                )}

                <p class="text-sm leading-relaxed text-ink-600 dark:text-paper-300 line-clamp-3">
                  {book.data.description}
                </p>

                {book.data.genres.length > 0 && (

                    {book.data.genres.map((genre) => (
                      <span class="rounded border border-paper-300/80 bg-paper-100/50 px-2 py-0.5 text-[11px] font-medium text-ink-700 dark:border-ink-700 dark:bg-ink-800/50 dark:text-paper-300">
                        {genre}
                      </span>
                    ))}
                  </div>
                )}
              </div>

              <!-- Retailer Links / Sample CTA -->
              <div class="mt-6 pt-4 border-t border-paper-200/90 dark:border-ink-800 flex flex-wrap items-center justify-between gap-2 text-xs">
                {book.data.sampleLink ? (
                  <a
                    href={book.data.sampleLink.href}
                    target="_blank"
                    rel="noopener noreferrer"
                    class="font-semibold text-accent-700 dark:text-accent-300 hover:underline"
                  >
                    {book.data.sampleLink.label} &rarr;
                  </a>

                  <span class="text-ink-500 dark:text-paper-400">Available across retailers</span>

                <div class="flex items-center gap-2">

                    <a

                      target="_blank"

                      class="rounded border border-paper-300 bg-white/70 px-2.5 py-1 text-[11px] font-semibold text-ink-800 hover:bg-paper-100 dark:border-ink-700 dark:bg-ink-800 dark:text-paper-200 dark:hover:bg-ink-700 no-underline"

S---
import Layout from "../../layouts/Layout.astro";
import { getCollection } from "astro:content";

const allBooks = (await getCollection("books", ({ data }) => !data.draft)).sort(
  (a, b) => {
    const dateA = a.data.publicationDate ? new Date(a.data.publicationDate).getTime() : 0;
    const dateB = b.data.publicationDate ? new Date(b.data.publicationDate).getTime() : 0;
    return dateB - dateA;
  }
);

const allSeries = await getCollection("series", ({ data }) => !data.draft);
const seriesMap = new Map(allSeries.map((s) => [s.id, s.data.title]));

const featuredBook = allBooks.find((b) => b.data.featured) ?? allBooks[0];
const catalogBooks = allBooks.filter((b) => b.id !== featuredBook?.id);
---

<Layout
  title="Books Showcase"
  description="Explore the fictional worlds, novels, and standalone stories by Alis Padasian."
>
  <div class="page-stack space-y-10 sm:space-y-12">
    <!-- Header -->
    <header class="page-header border-b border-paper-300/90 pb-6 dark:border-ink-700">
      <h1 class="page-title text-4xl font-semibold tracking-tight text-ink-950 dark:text-paper-50 sm:text-5xl">
        The Books Showcase
      </h1>
      <p class="page-description mt-3 max-w-2xl text-lg text-ink-700 dark:text-paper-300">
        Step into evocative worlds of secrets, fog-shrouded mysteries, and character-driven adventures.
      </p>
    </header>

    <!-- Lead / Gateway Book Feature (Hero Swap & Action) -->
    {featuredBook && (
      <section aria-labelledby="featured-book-heading" class="content-section">
        <div class="mb-3 flex items-center justify-between">
          <span class="inline-flex items-center gap-1.5 rounded-md border border-accent-300/60 bg-accent-50/70 px-2.5 py-1 text-xs font-semibold text-accent-800 dark:border-accent-700/50 dark:bg-accent-950/40 dark:text-accent-200">
            <span class="i-mdi:star text-xs" aria-hidden="true" />
            Recommended Gateway Title
          </span>
          {featuredBook.data.status === "forthcoming" && (
            <span class="rounded-md border border-amber-300/70 bg-amber-50 px-2.5 py-0.5 text-xs font-semibold text-amber-800 dark:border-amber-700/60 dark:bg-amber-950/40 dark:text-amber-300">
              Coming Soon
            </span>
          )}
        </div>

        <article class="surface-card rounded-2xl border border-paper-300/90 p-6 shadow-sm dark:border-ink-700 sm:p-8">
          <div class="grid gap-6 lg:grid-cols-3">
            <div class="lg:col-span-2 space-y-4">
              {featuredBook.data.seriesSlug && (
                <p class="font-mono text-xs font-semibold uppercase tracking-wider text-accent-700 dark:text-accent-300">
                  {seriesMap.get(featuredBook.data.seriesSlug) ?? featuredBook.data.seriesSlug}
                  {featuredBook.data.seriesOrder && ` 

---

 Book ${featuredBook.data.seriesOrder}`}
                </p>
              )}

              <h2 id="featured-book-heading" class="text-3xl font-bold tracking-tight text-ink-950 dark:text-paper-50 sm:text-4xl">
                {featuredBook.data.title}
              </h2>

              {featuredBook.data.tagline && (
                <p class="text-lg italic font-medium text-ink-800 dark:text-paper-200">
                  "{featuredBook.data.tagline}"
                </p>
              )}

              <p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-ink-700 dark:text-paper-300">
                {featuredBook.data.description}
              </p>

              <!-- Genre badges -->
              {featuredBook.data.genres.length > 0 && (
                <div class="flex flex-wrap gap-1.5 pt-2">
                  {featuredBook.data.genres.map((genre) => (
                    <span class="rounded-md border border-paper-300/80 bg-paper-100/70 px-2.5 py-0.5 text-xs font-medium text-ink-700 dark:border-ink-700 dark:bg-ink-800/60 dark:text-paper-300">
                      {genre}
                    </span>
                  ))}
                </div>
              )}

              <!-- Available Formats -->
              {featuredBook.data.formats.length > 0 && (
                <div class="pt-2 text-xs text-ink-600 dark:text-paper-400">
                  <span class="font-semibold text-ink-800 dark:text-paper-200">Available Formats:</span>{" "}
                  {featuredBook.data.formats.map((f) => f.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + f.slice(1)).join(" 

---

 ")}
                </div>
              )}

              <!-- Action CTAs: Sample & Purchase Links -->
              <div class="mt-6 flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3 pt-3 border-t border-paper-200 dark:border-ink-800">
                {featuredBook.data.sampleLink && (
                  <a
                    href={featuredBook.data.sampleLink.href}
                    target="_blank"
                    rel="noopener noreferrer"
                    class="inline-flex min-h-10 items-center gap-2 rounded-lg bg-accent-700 px-4 py-2 text-sm font-semibold text-white transition-colors hover:bg-accent-800 dark:bg-accent-600 dark:hover:bg-accent-500 no-underline"
                  >
                    <span class="i-mdi:book-open-page-variant text-base" aria-hidden="true" />
                    <span>{featuredBook.data.sampleLink.label}</span>
                  </a>
                )}

                {featuredBook.data.purchaseLinks.map((link) => (
                  <a
                    href={link.href}
                    target="_blank"
                    rel="noopener noreferrer"
                    class="action-link inline-flex min-h-10 items-center gap-1.5 rounded-lg border border-paper-300/90 bg-white/60 px-3.5 py-2 text-xs font-semibold text-ink-900 transition-colors hover:bg-paper-100 dark:border-ink-700 dark:bg-ink-800/50 dark:text-paper-100 dark:hover:bg-ink-700"
                  >
                    <span>{link.label}</span>
                    <span class="i-mdi:open-in-new text-xs" aria-hidden="true" />
                  </a>
                ))}
              </div>
            </div>

            <!-- Visual Cover Frame -->
            <div class="flex items-center justify-center rounded-xl bg-paper-100/60 p-6 dark:bg-ink-900/60 border border-paper-300/80 dark:border-ink-800">
              <div class="aspect-[2/3] w-48 rounded-lg bg-gradient-to-br from-accent-700 to-accent-950 p-4 shadow-md flex flex-col justify-between text-white text-center">
                <span class="text-xs uppercase tracking-widest text-accent-200">Alis Padasian</span>
                <h3 class="font-serif text-lg font-bold leading-tight">{featuredBook.data.title}</h3>
                <span class="text-[10px] text-accent-300">A Novel</span>
              </div>
            </div>
          </div>
        </article>
      </section>
    )}

    <!-- Complete Catalog Grid -->
    {catalogBooks.length > 0 && (
      <section aria-labelledby="catalog-heading" class="content-section space-y-6">
        <h2 id="catalog-heading" class="text-2xl font-bold tracking-tight text-ink-950 dark:text-paper-50">
          More Titles in the Catalog
        </h2>

        <div class="grid gap-6 md:grid-cols-2">
          {catalogBooks.map((book) => (
            <article class="surface-card flex flex-col justify-between rounded-xl border border-paper-300/90 p-6 dark:border-ink-700">
              <div class="space-y-3">
                <div class="flex items-center justify-between text-xs">
                  {book.data.seriesSlug ? (
                    <span class="font-mono text-accent-700 dark:text-accent-300 font-semibold">
                      {seriesMap.get(book.data.seriesSlug) ?? book.data.seriesSlug}
                      {book.data.seriesOrder && ` 

---

 #${book.data.seriesOrder}`}
                    </span>
                  ) : (
                    <span class="font-mono text-ink-500 dark:text-paper-400">Standalone</span>
                  )}
                  {book.data.status === "forthcoming" && (
                    <span class="rounded bg-amber-100 px-2 py-0.5 font-medium text-amber-800 dark:bg-amber-950/60 dark:text-amber-300 text-[11px]">
                      Forthcoming
                    </span>
                  )}
                </div>

                <h3 class="text-xl font-bold text-ink-950 dark:text-paper-50">
                  {book.data.title}
                </h3>

                {book.data.tagline && (
                  <p class="text-sm italic text-ink-700 dark:text-paper-300">
                    "{book.data.tagline}"
                  </p>
                )}

                <p class="text-sm leading-relaxed text-ink-600 dark:text-paper-300 line-clamp-3">
                  {book.data.description}
                </p>

                {book.data.genres.length > 0 && (
                  <div class="flex flex-wrap gap-1 pt-1">
                    {book.data.genres.map((genre) => (
                      <span class="rounded border border-paper-300/80 bg-paper-100/50 px-2 py-0.5 text-[11px] font-medium text-ink-700 dark:border-ink-700 dark:bg-ink-800/50 dark:text-paper-300">
                        {genre}
                      </span>
                    ))}
                  </div>
                )}
              </div>

              <!-- Retailer Links / Sample CTA -->
              <div class="mt-6 pt-4 border-t border-paper-200/90 dark:border-ink-800 flex flex-wrap items-center justify-between gap-2 text-xs">
                {book.data.sampleLink ? (
                  <a
                    href={book.data.sampleLink.href}
                    target="_blank"
                    rel="noopener noreferrer"
                    class="font-semibold text-accent-700 dark:text-accent-300 hover:underline"
                  >
                    {book.data.sampleLink.label} &rarr;
                  </a>
                ) : (
                  <span class="text-ink-500 dark:text-paper-400">Available across retailers</span>
                )}

                <div class="flex items-center gap-2">
                  {book.data.purchaseLinks.slice(0, 2).map((link) => (
                    <a
                      href={link.href}
                      target="_blank"
                      rel="noopener noreferrer"
                      class="rounded border border-paper-300 bg-white/70 px-2.5 py-1 text-[11px] font-semibold text-ink-800 hover:bg-paper-100 dark:border-ink-700 dark:bg-ink-800 dark:text-paper-200 dark:hover:bg-ink-700 no-underline"
                    >
                      {link.label}
                    </a>
                  ))}
                </div>
              </div>
            </article>
          ))}
        </div>
      </section>
    )}
  </div>
</Layout>
